title: Higher-moment constants require both prime arithmetic and zero geometry
claim: Across the three accounts, the leading constant in a higher zeta moment is not a single universal random-matrix number: it separates into a prime-local Euler-product factor and a residual geometric or zero-statistical factor. The hybrid Euler-Hadamard representation is the concrete bridge that keeps these contributions complementary, while polynomial lower-order refinements test whether their interaction has been retained beyond the leading monomial.
historical_or_program_relation: Random-matrix universality supplies a tractable model for the geometric factor, and the hybrid prime-zero program responds to the model's missing arithmetic factor by placing both sides in one cutoff-dependent representation.
limits: The factorization is conjectural for general higher moments, does not prove probabilistic independence of primes and zeros, and does not by itself determine exact lower-order coefficients or establish the zeta moment asymptotic.

title: Pair selection is the shared source of Gaussian moment structure
claim: Three different representations expose the same selective-compression mechanism: exponentiating a cumulant series reconstructs moments from primitive contributions, square support reduces expanded prime tuples to even multiplicity profiles, and explicit-formula arithmetic leaves prime pairings at main order. In each case, pair matchings retain a variance-scale statistic while suppressing more detailed configurations, explaining why Gaussian pairings and a quadratic moment exponent can emerge from otherwise different objects.
historical_or_program_relation: The random-matrix cumulant calculation supplies the ensemble-side Gaussian hierarchy, while prime-tuple and explicit-formula analyses identify arithmetic pairing mechanisms that can reproduce its main-order combinatorics without identifying the underlying objects pointwise.
limits: These are different averaging problems with different hypotheses. Main-order pairing does not prove a full Gaussian limit, does not retain repeated-prime corrections or arithmetic constants, and does not show that all higher-order correlations are negligible in every regime.

title: Moment order is a tunable lens on the extreme-value tail
claim: The moment index tunes how strongly an average weights rare large values. Layer-cake conversion makes that dependence explicit by balancing exponential moment weight against tail decay and locating the value band carrying most of the mass; large-k asymptotics then suggest an L-to-infinity route toward maximal order. This unifies moment growth, tail localization, and extreme-value prediction as different views of one order-sensitive transform.
historical_or_program_relation: Fixed-order moment conjectures provide the initial scalar summaries; tail estimates reveal where those summaries are accumulated, and large-k analysis asks whether the same family can be pushed far enough to control maximal order.
limits: A valid passage to maximal order requires estimates uniform as k grows with height. Fixed-k asymptotics or one-sided tail bounds are insufficient, and moments discard the locations and frequency of extreme values.

title: Multiscale prime blocks reconcile approximation length with moment budget
claim: Upper bounds for high zeta moments become feasible after log zeta is replaced by a prime-supported majorant and then split into blocks. The split allocates shorter admissible powers to longer, smaller-contribution blocks, while a synchronized horizontal shift cancels the zero term and time averaging reduces the remaining short polynomial moments to diagonal multiplicative combinatorics. The resulting architecture resolves the conflict between a long accurate approximation and the short total length required by high-moment mean values.
historical_or_program_relation: Prime-sum majorants turn the moment problem into polynomial mean values; blockwise truncation refines the earlier one-polynomial approach precisely where its length and tail requirements were incompatible.
limits: The construction is one-sided and depends on majorant validity, bad-set estimates, short-length inequalities, and parameter choices. It does not yield a matching lower bound or full distribution, and its constants can be greatly inflated by the terminal block scale.

title: Inverse-logarithmic separation is a common correlation-resolution boundary
claim: Shifted zeta moments and local characteristic-polynomial fields both change behavior when separation crosses their microscopic resolution. Under the matrix-size correspondence N approximately log T, the zeta threshold near 1/log T aligns with the CUE threshold near 1/N: below it, nearby evaluations share almost all logarithmic modes and behave like a higher-multiplicity insertion or a rank-one common fluctuation; above it, oscillation removes shared modes and correlations begin to decouple.
historical_or_program_relation: Shifted-moment bounds make the transition visible arithmetically, while harmonic-sum covariance and pathwise microscopic normalization supply matrix-side mechanisms for why that scale separates common from resolved information.
limits: The zeta statements include conditional or restricted moment inputs, and the CUE results concern a surrogate process. Matching scales does not identify zeta values with characteristic polynomials, determine extreme statistics, or establish independence immediately above the boundary.

title: Long moment approximations relocate the hard part into structured off-diagonal correlations
claim: Once a Dirichlet polynomial is long enough to model a higher zeta moment, its mean square retains interactions between nearby coefficient indices that a diagonal norm loses. Additive-divisor correlations are therefore the gate to the missing main terms, and multidimensional circle-method stratification by rational directions supplies intermediate objects that keep distinct near-resonant families from being averaged away.
historical_or_program_relation: The additive-divisor formulation isolates the correlation data absent from diagonal estimates; the multidimensional circle-method program systematizes Type II off-diagonal terms that earlier case-by-case treatments did not organize uniformly.
limits: The proposed correlation main terms and their residue or delta-method models remain conjectural in the needed generality. Rational-direction stratification organizes obligations but does not prove the higher-moment formula or validate every local Euler-product identification.

title: Small shifts resolve moment contributions before their singular limits coalesce
claim: Uniform small shifts act as generating coordinates for moment calculations: they separate derivative roles, expose companion pole contributions, and let unshifted formulas be recovered only after controlled coalescence. In long-polynomial fourth-moment calculations, organizing residues by swap order then closes the representation, because cutoff-dependent terms that survive within one class cancel only after zero-, one-, and two-swap strata are combined.
historical_or_program_relation: The exact shifted second-moment identity is the prototype; higher-moment work turns shifts into a bookkeeping and regularization interface, and the multidimensional correlation program interprets vanishing-discrepancy patterns as the arithmetic strata corresponding to swap order.
limits: The higher-moment descent assumes uniform shifted formulas and formula-sensitive residue calculations. Cancellation of cutoff artifacts is conditional evidence of architectural coherence, not an unconditional fourth-moment proof or permission to ignore individual length restrictions.

title: Mollified mean squares convert zero geometry into finite variational certificates
claim: Mollification creates a statistically controllable auxiliary function, and Littlewood-type reduction converts its zero count into the logarithm of an averaged squared magnitude. Differential-polynomial mean squares then compress the analytic estimate into a finite functional of test polynomials; a structured hyperbolic-sine trial profile and a balancing parameter turn the remaining optimization into an explicit energy certificate.
historical_or_program_relation: The classical critical-line proportion pipeline supplies the geometric-to-moment reduction, while later derivative-zero and distinct-zero work reuses the same interface with higher differential order and more explicit variational design.
limits: The output is a lower bound on a zero proportion, not RH or a location theorem for every zero. The certificate remains conditional on the imported mean-square estimate, admissible mollifier lengths, and trustworthy numerical specialization.

title: Pair-correlation energy is a two-way interface between zeros and prime gaps
claim: Fourier representation turns zero pair correlation into the weighted L2 energy of a one-parameter zero exponential sum. Beyond the unit-frequency boundary, evaluating that statistic demands shifted von Mangoldt correlations; in the reverse direction, scale-uniform control of the same zero energy bounds short-interval prime variance, so a long prime-free interval becomes detectable as excess nonnegative variance mass. The bridge is therefore bidirectional: fine prime correlations extend the zero statistic, and sufficiently strong zero statistics constrain prime gaps.
historical_or_program_relation: Montgomery's off-diagonal obstruction identifies the missing arithmetic input, while the prime-gap program repackages strengthened pair-correlation control as an energy estimate that can be compared with prime variance after logarithmic coordinate alignment.
limits: The transfers inherit RH and additional scale-uniform pair-correlation or prime-correlation hypotheses. Aggregate energy can certify existence of a prime configuration but does not locate it, and pair correlation alone does not determine the full consecutive-gap distribution.

title: Zero conditioning turns local collisions into derivative statistics and gap inputs
claim: A local eigenvalue collision can be represented by a canonical change of measure with a fourth characteristic-polynomial insertion. Independently, shrinking an offset in a conditioned characteristic-polynomial moment recovers derivative moments from the crossover profile. Hardy's real-valued critical-line representation then makes separate moments of Z and Z-prime usable as inputs to interval inequalities for large zero gaps. Together these form a representation pipeline from collision conditioning to derivative statistics to gap certificates.
historical_or_program_relation: Random-matrix conditioning supplies calculable local derivative-moment models, and the zeta gap program imports the resulting coefficient families when mixed zeta moments are unavailable.
limits: The matrix-to-zeta step is conjectural, and derivative-root radial distance, derivative magnitude at a zero, and a consecutive zeta gap are distinct observables. Conditional moment inputs yield limsup gap bounds, not a gap frequency or a proof of RH.

title: Short-interval moments and maxima become multiscale barrier problems
claim: On a typical short interval, log zeta is reorganized into nearly equal-variance prime blocks. A large value then means coordinated blockwise gains, while the moment integral is a partition function over the same field. Barrier events, mesh entropy, and a near/far second-moment decomposition determine whether enough nonredundant high points exist; varying interval scale changes the resulting moment and maximum exponents and exposes a freezing-type transition.
historical_or_program_relation: Prime-block reductions convert analytic maxima into probabilistic high-point counts, while the partition-function formulation places moment growth and extrema in one multiscale program rather than treating them as unrelated observables.
limits: These results concern typical randomized interval centers and one-sided high-probability or averaged statements, not the global maximum. Block approximations carry exceptional-set and derandomization costs, and a phase-transition profile does not by itself prove a complete freezing law or fluctuation distribution.

title: Shared Brownian modes separate scalar fluctuation from spatial chaos
claim: Minimum-type covariance is naturally represented as shared Brownian ancestry plus independent post-branch fluctuation. On mesoscopic zeta scales this separates a growing spatially constant Gaussian mode from a residual strictly logarithmic field, so normalization exposes a random scalar mass and a spatial chaos measure as different components. Block Brownian coupling carries the same spectral decomposition to CUE, while microscopic characteristic-polynomial normalization likewise isolates a rank-one common logarithmic fluctuation from bounded local geometry.
historical_or_program_relation: Gaussian-tree covariance gives the structural model, multiplicative-chaos analysis turns its mode split into a measure-level factorization, and CUE coupling supplies a controlled comparison object for the zeta field.
limits: The statements occur at different scales and normalizations, so the scalar mode and spatial chaos cannot be interchanged. Covariance matching and coupling do not identify zeta zeros with eigenvalues, imply RH, or determine the full nonlinear law without the stated regularization and topology controls.

title: Random-matrix moments acquire a concrete lattice-polytope geometry
claim: The characteristic-polynomial model turns the universal part of a zeta-moment conjecture into a tractable matrix moment. For truncated characteristic polynomials, that scalar moment is exactly represented by capacity-constrained pseudomagic-square counts; dilation then exposes a transportation-polytope volume as its leading scale. Changing from unitary to symplectic symmetry restricts the feasible matrices to a symmetric-even subspace, so the altered moment degree is read geometrically as a change in independent coordinates.
historical_or_program_relation: Random-matrix moment modeling supplies the universal surrogate, and combinatorial enumeration refines it by giving the surrogate coefficient an explicit discrete and geometric realization rather than leaving it as an unexplained scalar.
limits: The exact count requires its stated stable range and truncation conditions. Polytope volume discards lower-order lattice effects, does not supply the prime-dependent arithmetic factor, and does not prove the corresponding zeta or L-family moment conjecture.

title: Vertical norm transport replaces illegal deformation in fractional moments
claim: Fractional powers make a direct holomorphic deformation of zeta powers unavailable, but the needed comparison can be moved to norms rather than pointwise powers. Gabriel-type log convexity controls vertical Lp mass between boundary lines, while a rapidly decaying analytic kernel transports lower bounds from a line of absolute convergence toward the target line. The common move is to let analyticity act on an admissible localized function and only then recover the fractional moment quantity.
historical_or_program_relation: Convexity across vertical lines extends moment arguments beyond integer exponents, and kernel transport adapts the same analytic principle to short intervals where horizontal contour contributions must be suppressed explicitly.
limits: The two methods have different hypotheses and directions of inequality. They require decay or localization, careful boundary control, and parameter optimization; neither alone proves the full critical-line fractional-moment asymptotic.

title: Prime-square averages encode family symmetry as a shift of the value distribution
claim: A prime-square contribution that is negligible in one averaging environment can become a deterministic leading bias in a family. After centering, unitary, symplectic, and orthogonal families can share a logarithmic fluctuation scale while having different mean shifts. Trace and Frobenius-Schur indicators provide the representation-theoretic counterpart: low prime-power averages recover self-duality and pairing type, while root-number data remain a distinct statistic whose visibility depends on Fourier support.
historical_or_program_relation: Prime-polynomial tail analysis diagnoses the analytic center shift, and trace-formula family classification explains which coarse symmetry data those local averages encode and when a zero statistic can distinguish the candidate symmetry laws.
limits: A conditional one-sided normal-tail bound is not a Gaussian limit, and coarse indicators do not identify the full compact-group distribution. Symmetry type, functional-equation sign, and central-value nonvanishing are related but distinct, and insufficient Fourier support can make different families observationally indistinguishable.
